items.title: An abelian gerbe has an object over any neighbourhood on which the relevant cohomology vanishes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an abelian gerbe over a site has an object over an object of the site on which a cofinal system of coverings trivializes the relevant first cohomology and the second cohomology vanishes (statement lines 1676-1691). The proof is a complete descent argument: a covering with local objects is chosen and refined so that first cohomology vanishes on the pieces and their intersections (proof lines 1694-1700); the isom sheaves between local objects are identified as torsors and hence trivialized (proof lines 1701-1733); and the resulting failure of the cocycle condition is measured by a two-cocycle of the automorphism sheaf, which the Cech spectral sequence together with the vanishing shows to be a coboundary, after which the isomorphisms are corrected to give a descent datum (proof lines 1734-1748). The non-formal content is the passage from a trivialized comparison to a descent datum through the cohomological obstruction. The claim is H2: a structured descent argument with every input named.
